selection: First manifest row for each fixed class/domain; no correctness filtering

advisory.disclaimer: Decision support only. Consult a local agronomist before applying any product. Always follow product labels and local regulations.
advisory.dosage_notice: No universal dose is specified by this service. Use only products registered for the crop and disease; follow the local product label for concentration, rate, protective equipment, re-entry interval and pre-harvest interval. Consult a local agronomist.

treatment.symptoms: Large water-soaked grey-green lesions that turn brown/black quickly; white sporulation on leaf undersides in humid weather; firm brown fruit lesions.
treatment.chemical_treatment: Apply late-blight–labeled fungicides promptly when risk is high; protectants alone may be insufficient under severe pressure (follow the product label and local alerts).
treatment.organic_treatment: Copper products labeled for late blight plus immediate removal of infected plants; coverage must be thorough.
treatment.immediate_action: Bag and destroy infected plants (do not compost); notify nearby growers if outbreaks are regional.
treatment.prevention: Resistant cultivars where available, night-time leaf wetness reduction, and monitoring of late-blight forecast systems.
treatment.severity_guidance: Any confirmed late blight in humid weather is high severity — act the same day to limit spread.
sources: University of Minnesota Extension — Late Blight of Tomato, https://extension.umn.edu/diseases/late-blight, accessed 2026-10-11
Penn State Extension — Scouting and Identifying Tomato Diseases, https://extension.psu.edu/scouting-and-identifying-tomato-diseases, accessed 2026-10-11

treatment.cause: No pathogen; plant shows normal growth.
treatment.symptoms: Even green foliage without spots, mold, mosaic, curling, or stippling; normal flowering and fruit set.
treatment.chemical_treatment: No disease-control chemicals indicated by this prediction. Continue monitoring.
treatment.organic_treatment: No disease-control products indicated by this prediction. Continue cultural best practices.
treatment.immediate_action: Continue weekly scouting of lower leaves and leaf undersides.
treatment.prevention: Good airflow, drip irrigation, rotation, and resistant cultivars matched to local disease pressure.
sources: Clemson HGIC — Tomato Diseases & Disorders, https://hgic.clemson.edu/factsheet/tomato-diseases-disorders/, accessed 2026-10-11
